title: Tôi cần nước
summary: Different ways to say "I need water" in Vietnam, with the phrase to start with, reusable pieces, and related next steps.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Use this when drinking water or rinse water is the immediate need. This covers both bathroom and personal-need moments where you just need water fast. After the first answer, the related phrases help you handle the likely follow-up without starting over.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: Listen to each piece, then the whole phrase, so the rhythm feels connected instead of memorized word by word.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Tôi cần nước is the version to learn first for "I need water". Use this when drinking water or rinse water is the immediate need. Ask directly, then follow pointing or gestures; these moments usually need a quick practical answer.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use this when drinking water or rinse water is the immediate need. Use it in bathrooms, soap, paper, water, and basic personal needs when one clear sentence will work better than a long explanation.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: Some places may not have paper or soap available. Asking early avoids an awkward surprise.

sections.title: Local tip
sections.body: Ask directly and follow gestures. People may simply point you toward the right place.

sections.title: Explore next
sections.body: Use these next when the conversation moves one step forward.
